_comment: Windows packaging default engine overrides, applied by WhisperDictate.spec
when the parakeet.cpp runtime (packaging/parakeet-bin/parakeet.dll) is
staged for the build. Keys are the profile's current model; values replace
the engine/model/model_revision keys of matching profiles. Measured parity
(2026-10-07, .parity-scratch corpus): EN real WER 4.88% (parakeet f16 GGUF)
vs 7.32% (torch EN), no hotword regressions, GPU decode 4-8x faster. The
DE Nemotron GGUF measured 2.5% word drift vs the torch engine (the GGUF
bakes NeMo's default 240 ms lookahead instead of the 1.12 s setting the
transformers engine uses), so release DE stays on the torch engine.
2026-10-08: the EN source profile runs the becker engine on CPU (zero
VRAM; the fp32 parakeet graphs run at RTF 0.034 on the CPU EP), DE stays
becker on the int4 GPU export (~1.0 GiB; the CPU EP needs 8.6 s per 10 s
clip - the streaming encoder pays 35 chunk passes). becker.dll and the
model dirs are source-checkout-only assets, never staged for release, so
the overrides keep release builds on the resolver-shipped engines:
2026-10-13: the EN source profile switched to FluidVoice fluid-speech
mini (becker FluidTdt on the CPU EP; 100% text parity with the reference
ONNX script on the bench corpus, ~4.5% avg WER vs parakeet's 4.9%, 302
MB on disk, same zero-VRAM posture). The CUDA EP silently returns empty
text for its 2-bit MatMulNBits graphs, so EN must stay on CPU. Release
builds still ship the resolver engines (parakeet.cpp for EN). The former
parakeet-v3-onnx override entry was removed with the switch - overrides
must target a current profile model (tests/test_packaging.py guards this).
2026-10-24: the DE source profile switched to parakeet-v3-onnx on the CPU
EP (multilingual nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3; bench on the de parity
corpus ~4.2% WER vs nemotron35-int4's 7.4%, RTF 0.044 vs 0.071, 0 MB VRAM
instead of 644 MiB), so both profiles now hold zero VRAM. The nemotron
override is re-keyed to the new DE model dir; release builds keep the
resolver-shipped torch nemotron engine:
